partners.mechanism_chain: PROC (HGNC:9918) —DISRUPTS→ Protein C activation and anticoagulant activity (REACT:R-HSA-678952); PROS1 (HGNC:9922) —DISRUPTS→ Protein C activation and anticoagulant activity (REACT:R-HSA-678952); Protein C activation and anticoagulant activity (REACT:R-HSA-678952) —DECREASES→ Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-861780); Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-861780) —INCREASES→ Thrombophilia (HP:0002073); Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-861780) —INCREASES→ Venous thrombosis (HP:0002073). falsification.text: Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in PROC or PROS1 who do not exhibit thrombophilia, or conversely, identification of thrombophilia cases with no variants in PROC or PROS1, would challenge this proposed link. Furthermore, if genetic or functional studies demonstrate that Protein C and Protein S act through entirely independent and non-interacting pathways in regulating coagulation, this hypothesis would be falsified.
falsification.gnomad_variant: The presence of common benign variants in PROC and PROS1 in the general population (gnomAD > 1%) would not falsify the hypothesis, as these diseases are caused by rare pathogenic variants.

**Proposed mechanism:** Heterozygous mutation in PROC —DISRUPTS→ PROC (HGNC:9908); PROC (HGNC:9908) —DECREASES→ Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-V1-158343); Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-V1-158343) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombophilia (HP:0001416); Loss-of-function mutation in F10 —DISRUPTS→ F10 (HGNC:3771); F10 (HGNC:3771) —DECREASES→ Activated Factor X (CHEBI:57375); Activated Factor X (CHEBI:57375) —DECREASES→ Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-V1-158343); Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-V1-158343) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital factor X deficiency (HP:0011217). Mutations in PROC lead to insufficient Protein C activity, which normally inhibits activated Factor X (FXa) and activated Factor V (FVa) within the coagulation cascade. This leads to a pro-thrombotic state. Mutations in F10 lead to reduced production of functional FX, a key enzyme in the intrinsic and common pathways of the coagulation cascade, ultimately impairing thrombin generation and leading to bleeding tendency, but indirectly also affecting the feedback loops within the cascade.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a common variant in the PROC or F10 genes with a minor allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD, which is also implicated in causing either disease, would suggest that the proposed specific pathogenic variants are not the sole drivers or that the disease mechanism is more complex than a simple loss-of-function/haploinsufficiency. _(variant: rs753405149)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the distinct yet interconnected roles of PROC and F10 in the coagulation cascade is crucial for developing targeted therapies. For thrombophilia, anticoagulants are used, while for factor deficiencies, replacement therapy with purified factors or prothrombin complex concentrates is employed. Recognizing the shared pathway highlights potential for novel therapeutic strategies that modulate the cascade at different points.
